decisions.reason: As a low-cost complement to the core flooring business, the cleaning soap should be kept because after only one year there is still limited information about its full demand potential and little downside in maintaining the option.

The maintenance oil fits directly with the firm's installed base of wooden floors, and in a growing market it is sensible to keep this low-risk extension on the market while learning more about repeat demand.

Because this care product targets a specific floor-treatment segment within the firm's established offer, management would likely keep it as an inexpensive option until the market reveals whether it can build a stable niche.

The moisture-protection underlay strengthens the complete flooring system offer and likely has modest continuation costs, so it is worth keeping while the firm gathers more evidence on adoption by installers and trade buyers.
The high-density underlay foam is closely tied to the firm's core flooring applications, and with no clear negative signal yet the option value of staying in this adjacent segment remains attractive.

The oak parquet floor is close to the firm's main business and supports its design-led growth strategy, so despite higher carrying costs than accessories it should be kept because one year is too early to conclude that its value will not materialize.
